title: the tenth guru, the khalsa, the saint-soldier
hook: the tenth Guru, the Khalsa, the saint-soldier

segments.voice: Yesterday: the five Ks, from the uncut hair to the steel kara. Your line was reminders you can touch. What did the thing you chose remind you of? Day seventeen.
screen: `THE FIVE KS — REMINDERS YOU CAN TOUCH.`

segments.voice: Imagine being nine years old when your father leaves home knowing he may not come back. He's gone to the capital to stand up for the right of people from another faith to practice theirs. And he doesn't come back. He's executed. And now, at nine, the community turns to you. You are the Guru. That's how the tenth Guru's leadership began, in 1675. The boy grew into a poet, a warrior, a scholar of several languages, and the founder of the Khalsa. He carried a sword, and he wrote some of the most beautiful devotional poetry in Punjabi history. Today, the Guru who held both.
screen: `NINE YEARS OLD.` → `A FATHER WHO DOESN'T COME BACK.` → `YOU ARE THE GURU.`

segments.voice: Guru Gobind Singh, born in 1666, the tenth and last human Guru of the Sikhs. His father was the ninth Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur. Sikh tradition remembers that Guru Tegh Bahadur went to Delhi on behalf of Hindu Kashmiri pandits who were being pressed to convert, and was executed there by the Mughal authorities. Sikhs honor him as a martyr who gave his life for the freedom of others to worship. That memory shaped his son. Guru Gobind Singh taught that a person of faith should be two things at once. The Sikh phrase for it is sant sipahi: saint and soldier. Saint, because the inner life comes first: remembrance, humility, the name. Soldier, because when the weak are being crushed, a saint doesn't just look away. The sword on day sixteen, the kirpan, comes from exactly this. And the order matters. The saint comes first. A soldier with no saint in him is only violence. A saint with no courage may stand by while others suffer. In 1699, at a great gathering at Anandpur, the Guru founded the Khalsa, the community of the initiated, the ones who keep the five Ks. It's one of the most dramatic stories on this path, and we'll tell it properly later in the year. He also wrote poetry that Sikhs recite every day. He lost his father, and all four of his sons, to the violence of his time, and he's still remembered for chardi kala, rising spirits. And near the end of his life he made a decision that changed everything: there would be no eleventh human Guru. We'll come to that in three days.
screen: `THE TENTH GURU, BORN 1666.` · `A FATHER WHO DIED FOR OTHERS' FREEDOM.` · `SANT SIPAHI — SAINT AND SOLDIER.` · `THE SAINT COMES FIRST.` · then, large: `SWORD AND SAINT.`

segments.voice: Settle and breathe. Let one of your hands rest open on your lap: that's the saint, quiet, open, remembering. Let the other close into a gentle fist: that's the courage to stand up for someone. Feel both at once. Now think of one person in your life who might need you to stand up for them. Just hold them in mind, with both hands. The bell holds the time.
Guru Gobind Singh. The tenth Guru, founder of the Khalsa, poet and warrior: the saint-soldier. Seventeenth word.
Your line: sword and saint. Today, speak up once for someone who can't easily speak up for themselves, gently and without fear. Day seventeen.

screen: `DAY 17 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE STORIES OF THE GURUS.`

howItsDone: Sikhs honor Guru Gobind Singh as the tenth Guru and founder of the Khalsa, celebrate his birth each year, recite his compositions in daily prayers, and speak of the ideal of the sant sipahi, the saint-soldier.

pairs: where the great gathering was held

myth: Guru Gobind Singh was only a warrior
he was a poet and scholar too; Sikhs recite his writing every day.
his father was executed for defending others' freedom to worship
tradition remembers Guru Tegh Bahadur standing up for Kashmiri pandits.
in the saint-soldier, the soldier comes first
the saint comes first. courage serves the inner life, not the other way round.

fork.setup: you're a person of deep prayer, and you see the weak being crushed. what does the saint-soldier do?
options: pray, and stay out of it.
stand up for them, with the saint first.
fork.reveal: sant sipahi: saint first, then soldier. a saint doesn't look away, and a soldier without the saint is only violence.

original.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi script: the tenth Guru. Singh means lion, the name taken by Khalsa men.

trapdoor: what it means: the tenth Guru: poet, scholar and saint-soldier, who founded the Khalsa and held courage and devotion together.
what a scholar hears: he was born Gobind Rai, and tradition says he took the name Singh at the founding of the Khalsa in 1699. he also ended the line of human Gurus.

notes: Guru Tegh Bahadur's execution is described as Mughal and on behalf of Kashmiri pandits pressed to convert; this is the Sikh tradition's account. Confirm the careful framing ('Sikh tradition remembers').
Loss of all four sons (sahibzade) mentioned in one sentence without detail; confirm tone.
Name change Gobind Rai to Gobind Singh at the Khalsa's founding; confirm.
'Scholar of several languages' refers to his compositions in Braj, Persian and Punjabi; confirm.
The 1699 story is held for days 84–85 and not told here; the Guru Granth as Guru is day 20.
